status_summary: VA now lists the Office of Human Resources and Administration and the Office of Operations, Security, and Preparedness as separate staff offices with separate leaders. The President appointed Reginald G. A. Neal in December 2025 as Assistant Secretary for Operations, Security, and Preparedness, and in a written statement to a House Veterans' Affairs subcommittee on 2026-06-24 he said VA is completing a reorganization that gives that office its own Assistant Secretary, with Mark Engelbaum serving as Assistant Secretary for Human Resources and Administration. The statement ties the change to a unified chain of command for VA Police. No order or Federal Register notice of the separation and no effective date were found.

title: Consider separating VA's HR and Administration office from Security and Preparedness
uncertainties: The VA rule list on reginfo.gov (labeled Agency Rule List - 2026, 62 rules) lists no rulemaking on staff office structure, which would be internal. The separation rests on VA pages and a 2026-06-24 VA statement to Congress; no order, Federal Register notice or effective date was found, and the statement describes the reorganization as being completed. VA's stated purpose is a unified VA Police chain of command, not the staffing rationale the Mandate gives; the record reports alignment only. Some VA URLs still carry the combined office name. Whether the second Assistant Secretary position needed statutory change was not checked. Checked systematically on 2026-10-19.
